events.region: Barbour, WV; Harrison, WV; Randolph, WV; Taylor, WV; Upshur, WV
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Barbour County in northeastern West Virginia...
Northwestern Randolph County in northeastern West Virginia...
Northeastern Upshur County in northeastern West Virginia...
Harrison County in northern West Virginia...
Taylor County in northern West Virginia...

* WHEN...Until 430 PM EDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. It will take
several hours for all the water from these storms to work through
local drainage systems.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1013 AM EDT, Flooding is occurring in the warned area due to
thunderstorms last night. This includes locations along Middle
Fork Tygart Valley River where the automated gauge at Audra State
Park was in moderate flood. The latest gauge reading there was
11.65 feet and falling. At these stages the the campground and
roads within the park are flooded. In addition, lowl-lying
locations along the West Fork River from Shinnston to Enterprise
can expect flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Clarksburg, Grafton, Philippi, Audra State Park, Bridgeport,
Shinnston, Belington, Stonewood, Nutter Fort, Lumberport,
Anmoore, Enterprise, West Milford, Junior, Lost Creek,
Flemington, Galloway, Rosemont, Meadland and Century.
- This includes the following highways...
Interstate 79 between mile markers 109 and 128. Route 50 in West
Virginia between mile markers 69 and 82.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.region: Anderson, TN; Campbell, TN; Union, TN
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWMRX

The National Weather Service in Morristown has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Anderson County in east Tennessee...
Southeastern Campbell County in east Tennessee...
Southwestern Union County in east Tennessee...

* Until 115 PM EDT.

* At 1010 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2.5 inches of rain
have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour.
Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Rocky Top, Norris, Norris Dam State Park, Andersonville, Disney,
Big Ridge State Park, Norris Lake and Paulette.

This includes Interstate 75 in Tennessee between mile markers 122 and
133.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Red Lodge Foothills; Paradise Valley; Livingston Area; Beartooth Foothills; Absaroka/Beartooth Mountains; Southern Big Horn; Southeastern Carbon; Bighorn Canyon; Northern Carbon; Pryor/Northern Bighorn Mountains; Northeast Bighorn Mountains; Sheridan Foothills
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
The combination of a moist and unstable air mass with slow moving
thunderstorms capable of producing very heavy rain, will bring a risk
of flash flooding Wednesday afternoon and evening.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of south central Montana, including the following
areas, Absaroka/Beartooth Mountains, Beartooth Foothills, Bighorn
Canyon, Livingston Area, Northern Carbon, Paradise Valley,
Pryor/Northern Bighorn Mountains, Red Lodge Foothills, Southeastern
Carbon and Southern Big Horn and north central Wyoming, including
the following areas, Northeast Bighorn Mountains and Sheridan
Foothills.

* WHEN...From 1 PM MDT this afternoon through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Recent burn
scars, including the Robertson Draw and East Side south of Red
Lodge, and the Elk along the eastern slopes of the Bighorn
Mountains, are at risk of experiencing flash flooding and debris
flows.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Thunderstorms capable of producing very heavy rain are expected
this afternoon and evening. These storms may cause localized
flash flooding. Expect storms to begin developing over the
mountains by 1 or 2 pm.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Burns BLM; Steens Mountain; Southern Grasslands
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING ACROSS FAR
SOUTHEAST OREGON ZONES...

.Scattered thunderstorms are expected to develop near the Nevada
border and south-central Oregon this afternoon. The thunderstorms
are expected to be a mix of wet and dry. Expect gusty and erratic
winds up to 45 mph in the vicinity of these thunderstorms.

The National Weather Service in Boise has issued a Red Flag
Warning for lightning, which is in effect from 11 AM this morning
to 11 PM PDT this evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...In Oregon, Fire Weather Zones 670 Burns BLM,
671 Steens Mountain, and 672 Southern Grasslands.

* TIMING...From 11 AM this morning to 11 PM PDT this evening.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Scattered coverage with abundant lightning.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusty erratic winds up to 45 mph.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
